bottom_line: In patients hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within 10 days, 80 mg of atorvastatin daily vs 40 mg of pravastatin daily reduced the 2-year primary end point rate (22.4% vs 26.3%), reflecting a 16 percent reduction in the hazard ratio (95 percent confidence interval, 5 to 26 percent).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, the intensive regimen (2-year primary end point 22.4%) was associated with fewer primary end point events than the standard regimen (26.3%), with a reported 16 percent hazard reduction (95 percent confidence interval, 5 to 26 percent). The results also show different achieved LDL levels (median 62 vs 95 mg per deciliter) and more ALT elevations >3× ULN with high-dose atorvastatin (3.3% vs 1.1%); they do not establish the mechanism of benefit or isolate whether LDL lowering vs other differences between statins caused the outcome difference.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind comparison of standard-dose pravastatin vs high-dose atorvastatin after recent ACS.
major_points.quote: compared 40 mg of pravastatin daily (standard therapy) with 80 mg of atorvastatin daily (intensive therapy).

major_points.text: Population enrolled: ACS hospitalization within preceding 10 days; total N=4162.
major_points.quote: We enrolled 4162 patients who had been hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days

major_points.text: Primary end point was a composite including death, MI, unstable angina requiring rehospitalization, revascularization ≥30 days, and stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary end point was a com- posite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, documented unstable angina re- quiring rehospitalization, revascularization (performed at least 30 days after randomiza- tion), and stroke.

major_points.text: Median achieved LDL levels differed substantially between groups during treatment.
major_points.quote: The median LDL cholesterol level achieved during treatment was 95 mg per deciliter (2.46 mmol per liter) in the standard-dose pravastatin group and 62 mg per deciliter (1.60 mmol per liter) in the high-dose atorvastatin group (P<0.001).

major_points.text: Primary end point at 2 years favored atorvastatin with a reported hazard reduction and CI; noninferiority/equivalence criterion was not met.
major_points.quote: rates of the primary end point at two years were 26.3 percent in the prav- astatin group and 22.4 percent in the atorvastatin group, reflecting a 16 percent reduc- tion in the hazard ratio in favor of atorvastatin (P=0.005; 95 percent confidence interval, 5 to 26 percent).

major_points.text: Safety: more ALT elevations >3× ULN with atorvastatin; no rhabdomyolysis in either group.
major_points.quote: The percentages of patients who had elevations in alanine aminotransferase lev- els that were more than three times the upper limit of normal were 1.1 percent in the pravastatin group and 3.3 percent in the atorvastatin group (P<0.001).
